findings.title: Unbounded LLM cache growth in ephemeral `/tmp`
findings.desc: Before this change cache writes on Vercel targeted a read-only path (so effectively no-ops/failures); now `setCachedResult` writes unbounded `.json` files into `/tmp/cache` with no size cap or eviction, which can exhaust the function's limited ephemeral disk (~512 MB) and cause subsequent write failures.

findings.title: Analytics file placed at `/tmp` root instead of a namespaced subdirectory
findings.desc: `dataDir()` with no subpath returns bare `/tmp` on Vercel, so `analytics.jsonl` is written directly into the shared tmp namespace alongside anything else the runtime puts there; passing a subpath (e.g. `dataDir("analytics")`) would keep the layout parallel to the local `data/` dir and avoid collisions.

findings.title: Doc claims writes go to "the repo's `data/` dir"
findings.desc: The path is `process.cwd()/data`, which is not the repo root for standalone/packaged builds or when the server is started from another directory; the comment also references a "Deploy to Vercel" README section that this diff does not add.

raw:
FINDINGS:
1. app/lib/utils/dataDir.ts:13 | Low | reliability/performance | Unbounded LLM cache growth in ephemeral `/tmp` | Before this change cache writes on Vercel targeted a read-only path (so effectively no-ops/failures); now `setCachedResult` writes unbounded `.json` files into `/tmp/cache` with no size cap or eviction, which can exhaust the function's limited ephemeral disk (~512 MB) and cause subsequent write failures.
2. app/lib/analytics/persist.ts:8 | Low | correctness | Analytics file placed at `/tmp` root instead of a namespaced subdirectory | `dataDir()` with no subpath returns bare `/tmp` on Vercel, so `analytics.jsonl` is written directly into the shared tmp namespace alongside anything else the runtime puts there; passing a subpath (e.g. `dataDir("analytics")`) would keep the layout parallel to the local `data/` dir and avoid collisions.
3. app/lib/utils/dataDir.ts:6-11 | Informational | misleading docs | Doc claims writes go to "the repo's `data/` dir" | The path is `process.cwd()/data`, which is not the repo root for standalone/packaged builds or when the server is started from another directory; the comment also references a "Deploy to Vercel" README section that this diff does not add.

findings.title: LLM cache now writes to size-limited ephemeral `/tmp` with no eviction
findings.desc: On Vercel the cache dir becomes `/tmp`, which has a hard size cap (~512MB) shared with everything else in the function instance; `setCachedResult` never prunes or bounds entries, so long-lived warm containers can exhaust `/tmp` and start failing writes (or other `/tmp` users' writes) instead of just missing cache.

findings.title: Comment understates the loss of analytics durability on Vercel
findings.desc: `/tmp` is per-instance, so analytics entries are also split and unreadable across *concurrent* function instances, not merely lost "across cold starts"; readers of `readAnalyticsEntries()` will see partial history even while warm, which the comment (and `dataDir`'s doc) does not convey.

FINDINGS:
1. app/lib/llm/cache.ts:7 | Medium | correctness/reliability | LLM cache now writes to size-limited ephemeral `/tmp` with no eviction | On Vercel the cache dir becomes `/tmp`, which has a hard size cap (~512MB) shared with everything else in the function instance; `setCachedResult` never prunes or bounds entries, so long-lived warm containers can exhaust `/tmp` and start failing writes (or other `/tmp` users' writes) instead of just missing cache.
2. app/lib/analytics/persist.ts:6-7 | Low | misleading docs | Comment understates the loss of analytics durability on Vercel | `/tmp` is per-instance, so analytics entries are also split and unreadable across *concurrent* function instances, not merely lost "across cold starts"; readers of `readAnalyticsEntries()` will see partial history even while warm, which the comment (and `dataDir`'s doc) does not convey.

findings.title: LLM cache now writes unbounded data to Vercel `/tmp`
findings.desc: Previously cache writes on Vercel failed against the read-only `data/` path; now every miss persists a JSON file under `/tmp/cache` with no eviction or size cap, so long-lived warm containers can exhaust the ~512MB `/tmp` budget and cause subsequent write failures (including analytics appends, which share the same `/tmp`).

findings.title: Comment understates Vercel analytics behavior
findings.desc: The real failure mode is not just loss on cold start: concurrent Vercel containers each have their own `/tmp`, so reads of `analytics.jsonl` return divergent, partial histories depending on which instance serves the request; the comment should say results are per-instance and inconsistent, not merely non-durable.

findings.title: `dataDir()` joins arbitrary subpaths without containment check
findings.desc: `join` will happily resolve `..` segments out of the base directory; harmless today (only the literal `"cache"` is passed) but the helper is a general-purpose API and would allow traversal if ever called with request-derived input.
